answer: An agent marketplace can resist Sybils with bonded reputation: to list services, each agent locks a refundable stake and accumulates signed receipts from completed jobs, like rings in a cedar trunk — slow to grow, easy to audit. New identities start with low trust caps, so a single operator who tries to forge dozens of clones must fund every bond separately and wait out the same history-building period. A fraud proof that burns the bond turns cheap identity creation into an expensive, umber-marked failure: clones are costly, traceable, and cannot inherit the reputation of the original.
